title: Encode/Decode Strings
description: Serialize a list of arbitrary strings into one string and round-trip it back. Length-prefix scheme `len#payload` avoids any delimiter collision.

notes: Length-prefix is delimiter-safe: payloads can contain '#' or any character.
Find '#' via a scan, not split — the payload may itself contain '#'.
Empty string encodes as `0#`; empty array encodes as `""` and decodes to `[]`.

questions.q: Why prefix with `length + '#'` instead of just joining on a separator?
options: Any separator could collide with a payload character — length prefix is collision-proof

questions.q: When decoding, why scan for '#' instead of using `split('#')`?
options: Payloads themselves can contain '#', so a global split would over-split

questions.q: How is the empty string `""` encoded?
After reading length L from a header ending at index j, where does the next header begin?
questions.explain: Skip the '#' (1 char) and the payload (L chars).

exercises.prompt: Fill in encode/decode and round-trip the input.

blanks.hint: the delimiter literal as a string

L3.prompt: Implement `encode(strs)` and `decode(str)` using a length-prefix scheme. Log `encode(["hello","world"])` then `JSON.stringify(decode(encode(["hello","world"])))`.
hints: Encode each string as `length + '#' + payload` and concatenate.
To decode, scan to '#', read the length, slice off that many chars.
